alex_support: Hi @sara_acme — saw your note about the invoice showing ~18% higher token usage for your private cluster in us-east-2. Can you confirm this is the same project id you synced last week?

sara_acme: yep same project id: acme-frontend-prod. billing dashboard shows 4.3M tokens for the month, ledger shows 5.1M. we only had a short maintenance window last Tue (20:45-21:05) where we upgraded the node pool.

alex_support: thanks. quick summary of what we suspect: on-prem metering agent buffered requests during the node restart, then replayed them, but some messages appear to have been duplicated at the collector side because of overlapping replay windows + sequence checkpoint not advancing. looking for logs and a minimal reproducer.

vik_infra: adding from infra side — during the restart the agent used the default buffer TTL (30m) and aggressive resend (backoff=linear, attempts=5). We saw a short NTP step on the host (-120s) from the kernel logs during reboot. That can cause seq/ts overlap if client replay uses wallclock-based windows.

kim_metering: pinging metering eng. If duplicates happened we should see identical request ids or sequence ids in the collector. Can @telemetry_bot pull the last 2k event ids we received from acme-frontend-prod between 1795860000 and 1795865000?

telemetry_bot: Sure — attaching a sample result (first 8 lines):
```
2026-03-10T20:46:12Z acme-frontend-prod req_id=6b8f... seq=345678 ts=1795860372 tokens=42
2026-03-10T20:46:13Z acme-frontend-prod req_id=6b8f... seq=345679 ts=1795860373 tokens=38
2026-03-10T20:46:13Z acme-frontend-prod req_id=6b8f... seq=345678 ts=1795860373 tokens=42  # duplicate seq with incremented ts
2026-03-10T20:46:15Z acme-frontend-prod req_id=7c9a... seq=345680 ts=1795860375 tokens=15
2026-03-10T20:46:16Z acme-frontend-prod req_id=7c9a... seq=345680 ts=1795860396 tokens=15  # replayed later
```

alex_support: that pattern matches duplicate delivery rather than miscounting tokens locally. Notice same seq appears twice with slightly different timestamps. If collector doesn't dedupe by req_id+seq we count both.

kim_metering: two follow-ups: (1) Do you have agent logs showing when it considered a chunk committed vs acknowledged? (2) What's your dedupe policy at the collector? Current default dedupe window is 2m keyed by (project, req_id, seq). If the agent replay moved the ts forward beyond 2m because of NTP step/resend, we can miss dedupe.

sara_acme: i can share agent logs. attaching snippet: 
```
[2026-03-10T20:45:58Z] INFO buffer: flushed 1024 events to outgoing queue
[2026-03-10T20:46:00Z] WARN comms: send failed, retrying attempt=1
[2026-03-10T20:46:30Z] INFO comms: replaying buffered events starting seq=345670
[2026-03-10T20:47:05Z] INFO buffer: all events acked
```

vik_infra: host /var/log/messages shows NTP step at 20:46:14: `kernel: clock: step by -120s` — so replay overlaps earlier window.

alex_support: root cause hypothesis: agent buffered during node recycle, then host NTP step moved clock back ~2m, agent retransmit used wallclock-based timestamps causing some events to appear with new timestamps that overlap previous ones when collector applies a short dedupe TTL. Combined with collector dedupe keyed only by req_id+seq within 2m, some duplicates escaped dedupe (because one copy had ts older than window), leading to double counting.

kim_metering: mitigation options: 
- short term: increase collector dedupe window for your project to 10m and run a reconciliation to collapse duplicates found by req_id+seq. We can run a backfill job to dedupe events between 1795860000-1795865000.
- medium term: change agent to attach immutable ingestion-id (UUID per request) and include origin_timestamp + monotonic_seq to avoid wallclock reliance.
- long term: agent should checkpoint using monotonic counters persisted across restarts and use monotonic-based replay windows. We'll file a patch for v0.12.3.

jordan_csm: flagging for billing — will delay invoice adjustments until we confirm the reconciliation. Customer requires an itemized diff.

sara_acme: thanks. to confirm: can you run the backfill dedupe and share the delta? Also what can we do on our side to minimize risk in future maintenance windows?

alex_support: next steps I propose: 
1) Permission from Acme to run the dedupe backfill (I have a job ready but need approval).
2) Temporarily bump dedupe window for the project to 10m (will reduce chance of double counting for similar incidents).
3) We will run reconciliation and produce an itemized re-count for the billing team.
4) Agent config recommendations for you: set buffer.ttl=10m (instead of 30m) and enable monotonic_seq=true if you can run the latest agent binary; if not, set resend.backoff=exponential and max_attempts=3.

kim_metering: i opened GH issue #5482 for the agent monotonic checkpoint work and assigned to eng-runtime. ETA preliminary patch: 2 weeks. We'll also add a safety dedupe that considers identical payload hash if req_id/seq matches within 15m.

sara_acme: grant given for backfill. please run it and share the result. also i'll push a maintenance note to our infra schedule to prefer a quiesce window before restarts.

alex_support: thanks — running backfill now, i'll post results in this thread when it's done. tagging @jordan_csm for billing follow-up. :thumbsup:

telemetry_bot: backfill job started job_id=bf-20260310-01; estimating 2min for 20k events.

(10m later)

telemetry_bot: backfill job completed job_id=bf-20260310-01; duplicates collapsed: 185, tokens reclaimed: 7421. New ledger delta: -7421 tokens.

alex_support: confirmed — billing team, please apply credit of 7,421 tokens (or equivalent USD) to acme-frontend-prod invoice for Mar 2026. I'll attach the backfill audit log and the list of deduped req_ids.

jordan_csm: billing will issue a credit memo and updated invoice within 3 business days. sending copy to @sara_acme when posted.

sara_acme: appreciate the quick turnaround. we'll follow the agent config suggestions and report back after our next maintenance run.

vik_infra: quick note for docs — we should add a KB entry describing NTP interactions, monotonic seqs, and recommended buffer/resend settings. low-priority ticket created.

kim_metering: thx team. keeping this open until the patch lands and the KB is published.

alex_support: closing loop here — marking as resolved for now; reopen if any new spikes.
